Introduction

This handbook is the written half of what a relief driver otherwise learns by asking. It is revised once a year, in the week the school services change, and it has never been shorter than forty pages.

The depot

The depot gate is the only way in and out, and it is wide enough for one bus. Everything about the morning order of departure follows from that single fact.

Livery

Two liveries are in service. The school pair carry the sponsor's colours, which is an arrangement Northwind Traders renews each September without anyone having to ask.

Radio

The radio reaches everywhere except the valley, where it has never reached and where the handbook has always said to use a telephone instead.

Relief drivers

A relief driver is expected to know the eastern loop before taking the western one, because the western loop leaves the valley and the radio does not follow.

Lost property

Lost property goes in the cupboard by the gate and is kept for a month. Umbrellas are kept for a week, because the cupboard is not large.

Weather

Snow closes the valley. Nothing else does, including the two days a year the river comes over the road at the market.

Closing the loop

The last eastern departure waits three minutes for the last western arrival, every night, whether or not anybody is changing. It is the one rule in here nobody has ever argued with.
